lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Rebuilt the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards around per-sensor error budgets, cutting mean time to detect incidents from 40 to 12 minutes.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Raised defect localization on a 120-case benchmark from 82% to 94% by dispatching tasks to role-specialized sub-agents with isolated prompts, toolsets and contexts.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Add a short target-oriented summary only if needed.
items.because: A summary could help frame the transition for broader software roles.

items.says: Make the technology stack more visible.
items.because: Several bullets describe important technologies without naming the relevant infrastructure, frameworks, databases, queues, monitoring tools, or deployment environment.

items.says: Define specialized terms at least once.
items.because: Terms such as 'domain adapter,' 'assistant-only loss masking,' 'GRPO,' 'budgeted context layers,' and 'stream completion' may be opaque to general hiring managers.

items.says: Clarify measurement methodology for metrics.
items.because: Reviewers may ask whether metrics came from production, offline testing, a fixed benchmark, or manually evaluated samples.

items.says: Use consistent date and punctuation formatting.
items.because: Bullets wrap awkwardly and hyphenation such as 'dead-letter' breaks across lines.

items.says: Consider adding links to relevant work.
items.because: Direct links to repositories or demos are more useful than a general code profile.

items.says: Avoid unexplained company placeholders in the actual resume.
items.because: Recognizable company names or a short description can improve context.

items.says: Make the code URL a complete clickable URL, including the protocol.
items.because: Recruiters should be able to reach and verify you quickly.

items.says: Consider adding LinkedIn if it is current and aligned with the resume.
items.because: A general code profile is less useful than direct links to relevant projects.

items.says: Ensure your email and phone number are visually secondary to your name.
items.because: Not all contact info should have equal emphasis.

items.says: Make the expected status visually unambiguous.
items.because: The master's degree is current and directly relevant.

items.says: Add a selective line for specialization, thesis area, or advanced courses if relevant.
items.because: The resume does not show what part of computer engineering supports your ML and agent-systems work.

items.says: Consider adding GPA only if it is strong and relevant.
Consider adding honors, class rank, or relevant specialization only if notable.
items.because: The degree supports your background, but the resume should emphasize recent work.

items.says: Keep this entry compact if your graduate degree is now the main credential.
items.because: Recent work should be emphasized over older education.

items.says: Verify that date formats, geographic labels, and institution formatting are consistent.
Consider moving Education below Experience for full-time engineering roles.
items.because: Your professional experience is stronger evidence of ability.

items.says: Clarify what 'branch' means: model path, workflow, product feature, or service branch.
items.because: 'Branch' and 'pending-case backlog' are domain-specific.

items.says: Clarify whether '800+ sensor signals per case' means all signals are processed or selected among.
items.because: Readers need to understand the system and measurement basis.

items.says: State whether the 68% backlog reduction was measured against a comparable pre-launch period and whether other operational changes contributed.
items.because: The result is compelling only if the metric is attributable to the feature.

items.says: Keep 'eight weeks after launch' only if the metric is genuinely attributable; otherwise, make the attribution more cautious.
Define 'diagnostic accuracy' and specify the evaluation method.
items.because: A hiring manager needs to understand what changed and why the comparison is valid.

items.says: Explain 'domain adapter' briefly or use a more recognizable term.
items.because: The technical method is dense.

items.says: Retain 'assistant-only loss masking' only if it was central to the improvement.
items.because: Otherwise, the technique may distract from the result.

items.says: Clarify the baseline and whether the comparison used the same evaluation set and inference procedure.
Clarify whether the three specialists and reviewer are agents, models, services, or human roles.
items.because: 'Reviewer disagreement' can sound subjective unless its definition is clear.

items.says: Explain what 'in-scope signals' means operationally.
Specify how reviewer disagreement was measured and whether the reduction affected accuracy, review time, or only agreement.
Spell out GRPO once if the resume may be read by general software recruiters.
items.because: It introduces several claims that invite questions about reward design and tradeoffs.

items.says: Identify whether the reward penalty reduced unnecessary tool calls without increasing failure, abstention, or retry rates.
Clarify the meaning of 'equal accuracy': equal to the SFT baseline, statistically indistinguishable, or exactly the same on the benchmark.
Reconsider including both the 18% tool-call reduction and 5% latency reduction if the latency improvement is modest and not central.
Name the major evaluation dimensions more concretely if space allows.
items.because: The value lies in demonstrating release protection.

items.says: Clarify whether 'catching 2 accuracy regressions' means the harness detected them before deployment or merely surfaced them for investigation.
State whether the 14 checkpoints represented model versions, adapter versions, or training checkpoints.
Clarify your ownership: documentation alone, or did you define, validate, and operationalize the rules?
items.because: Adoption by reviewers is less concrete than your other metrics.

items.says: Replace the ambiguous 'who' relationship so it is clear the runbook was adopted by the on-call team.
If the runbook reduced escalation errors or review time, add that result; otherwise keep the current adoption result.
Put the most strategically relevant bullets first.
items.because: Readers should immediately see production impact, model quality, systems design, and evaluation ownership.

items.says: Make sure the internship title does not imply more ownership than you had.
items.because: Use the bullets to demonstrate ownership rather than relying on the title.

items.says: Add the primary tools or infrastructure somewhere in the section if they are absent from Skills.
Clarify whether you designed the error budgets, implemented the instrumentation, or only rebuilt the dashboards.
items.because: The causal link between dashboards and detection time should be explicit.

items.says: Specify the monitoring stack if it is relevant to the role.
Explain whether the reduction in mean time to detect came from better dashboards, alerting changes, or both.
Identify the caching and batching layer if relevant.
items.because: Added detail would make the performance claim more credible and reproducible.

items.says: Clarify whether the 200 ms threshold was a target, an enforced service-level objective, or a CI performance gate.
State whether load tests represented production traffic patterns.
Replace 'maintained' with a more specific description of your ownership or improvement.
items.because: 'Maintained' can sound routine, while the measurable release improvement suggests meaningful engineering work.

items.says: Clarify how automated regression checks shortened the release cycle.
Identify what kinds of regressions were tested.
Name the event-queue technology if it is recognizable and relevant.
items.because: The impact is described in operational language that may be hard for non-robotics readers to interpret.

items.says: Clarify what 'nightly backlogs' means operationally and whether removing them improved dispatch reliability or startup time.
Mention whether you handled rollout, compatibility, monitoring, or failure recovery.
Consider ordering the bullets by relevance to the job.
items.because: The section should communicate your level of autonomy.

items.says: Add one bullet or detail involving design ownership if you had it.
items.because: The current section emphasizes implementation and operations more than architecture.

items.says: Make clear whether this is an independent project, open-source project, research project, or startup-related work.
items.because: The reader needs context about scope and public availability.

items.says: Add a repository or demo link if public.
Verify that 'Owner' accurately reflects your role and does not imply a larger team or product than exists.
Consider changing the date display only if 'Present' is not accurate.
Define 'defect localization' and the benchmark’s task more clearly.
items.because: Benchmark provenance and experimental controls determine how credible it appears.

items.says: State whether the benchmark was self-created, public, or internal.
Clarify the comparison point and whether the same model, tools, and evaluation budget were used.
Clarify what 'working context' includes and how it was measured.
items.because: 'Context' and 'conversation grew 100x' could be interpreted several ways.

items.says: Explain what 'raw conversation grew 100x' refers to—tokens, message count, or total input size.
Consider whether the 100-turn stress test is enough to support the claim; if you ran multiple trials, include that context.
Explain what kinds of pools were separated and where the deadlocks occurred.
items.because: A measurable reliability or performance outcome would make it stronger.

items.says: Clarify whether '50-way fan-out' represents a test condition, production workload, or maximum supported configuration.
Include a reliability or throughput result if you have one.
Clarify whether you were an open-source contributor, research collaborator, or maintainer.
items.because: A link would let reviewers verify the contribution.

items.says: Add the repository or pull-request link if public.
Consider placing this project above Agent Runtime Suite only for evaluation, research, or safety-oriented roles.
items.because: Otherwise the runtime project is probably more directly relevant.

items.says: Clarify whether you authored the metrics, implemented them, or integrated existing metrics.
items.because: The important achievement is that your work became part of the project’s standard release process.

items.says: Explain what 'default benchmark for every release' means in practical terms.
If the framework has meaningful adoption, include that only if you can substantiate it.
Define 'injected degradation' more clearly in the resume’s surrounding context.
items.because: Without describing the experiment structure, readers may not know what the 0.89 correlation establishes.

items.says: Explain whether the Kendall correlation was calculated across systems, reports, perturbation levels, or another unit.
Clarify whether higher correlation means better evaluator validity in your setup.
Clarify whether these defects were found in your own framework or in the upstream open-source project.
items.because: The reader should understand the scope and impact of the fixes.

items.says: Identify the practical consequences of the defects if they affected benchmark validity or reproducibility.
State whether your fixes were also upstreamed, if that is true.
Move Git out of Programming and into a tools or development category.
items.because: Git is not a programming language.

items.says: Add technologies demonstrated in the experience if they are relevant to your target roles.
items.because: The current list understates your engineering stack.

items.says: Avoid listing technologies that you only encountered superficially.
Categorize 'agent evaluation' as a capability rather than a technology, or place it in a more appropriate category.
items.because: The current category is relevant but compressed.

items.says: Spell out or explain GRPO once somewhere if the target audience is mixed.
Add only the major frameworks and techniques you can discuss deeply in an interview.
Consider separating model training, evaluation, and agent infrastructure if you have enough relevant tools to justify it.

Include skills that are already evidenced by your bullets, such as distributed systems, model evaluation, inference optimization, observability, CI/CD, or message queues—but only if you can name the concrete technologies or methods.
items.because: The Skills section should reinforce the strongest evidence in the resume.

items.says: Do not add soft skills, generic terms such as 'problem solving,' or a long list of unrelated tools.
Put the most job-relevant skills first and tailor this section for each application.
items.because: Recruiters and applicant-tracking systems often scan the Skills section quickly.
